worlds.name: Field Notes
worlds.summary: A researcher's brand: careful observation of how teams actually behave.
worlds.naming_direction: Language from fieldwork and observation: notes, samples, findings.

sample_names.name: Findings
sample_names.rationale: What you learn about a teammate before you commit.

sample_names.name: Observed
sample_names.rationale: Short, and it implies evidence rather than opinion.

worlds.tagline_direction: Observations stated as findings, with the sample size implied.
voice_rules: Report what happened before interpreting it.
Prefer a small true number to a large vague one.
Let the reader draw the conclusion.
worlds.voice_sample_line: Across four projects, the people who replied within a day were the ones who finished.

typography.rationale: Reads like a published finding rather than an ad.
Compact and legible for dense notes.

composition: Two-column layout with a wide margin for notes
worlds.audience_perception: Thoughtful and slightly academic — trustworthy, possibly dry for a first-year student.
risks: Understated to the point of forgettable
opportunities: Positions the product as evidence, not opinion
Gives the brand something to publish
obvious_ideas_rejected: A data-dashboard world of graphs and KPIs — the obvious home for anything measured, and it reduces people to metrics.
A study-hall aesthetic of coffee and highlighters — the standard student stock imagery.

worlds.name: The Handshake
worlds.summary: A brand built on the moment two people agree, treated as something formal and worth marking.
worlds.naming_direction: Words for agreements made between equals: terms, pacts, word, shake.

sample_names.name: On Terms
sample_names.rationale: Names the agreement without legal coldness.

sample_names.name: Word
sample_names.rationale: What a student gives, and what this product keeps track of.

worlds.tagline_direction: Short declarations about what each person owes the other.
voice_rules: Address both sides of the agreement, never just the user.
Name the obligation before the benefit.
worlds.voice_sample_line: You said you would take the backend. That is now written down, and so is theirs.

typography.rationale: Plain civic sans that keeps the terms readable.

imagery: Two hands cropped tight, never a stock handshake
composition: Centred, symmetrical layouts like a certificate
Generous margins and one rule per section
worlds.audience_perception: Serious and a little old-fashioned — makes the commitment feel real, may feel heavy for a two-day hackathon.
risks: The certificate look is close to parody if overdone
opportunities: Turns the agreement into a shareable artefact
Distinct from every app in the category
obvious_ideas_rejected: A contract-and-compliance world of legal grey — the obvious way to show agreement, and nobody signs it.
A pinky-promise, playful world — the cute inversion, which undercuts being left with the work.
